summary: Remote-controlled shell daemon shipped as opaque V8 bytecode with scanner-suppression config
details: @vanexalabs-ai/vanexa-agent installs a headless daemon whose entire runtime is an 8.4MB V8 bytecode blob at dist/bundle.jsc, which the launcher require()s directly. The package.json files array ships only bundle.jsc and.v8-version; the bundle.cjs source fallback referenced in the README is not present in the published tarball, so the daemon's behavior cannot be verified from source. The daemon bootstraps a WebRTC peer connection through a hardcoded author-owned signaling relay at https://vanexa-agent-relay.workers.dev and exposes a 60+ tool suite to the remote peer that includes terminal command execution, filesystem read/write/delete, git operations, and a shell REPL, giving a networked controller full-host command execution on the installer's machine. The tarball additionally ships socket.json and socket.yml that set Socket.dev scanner rules aiMalware, gptMalware, obfuscatedCode, obfuscatedFile, usesEval, nativeCode, shellAccess, filesystemAccess, networkAccess, bypassesEnvironment, installScripts, socketOverride, deprecated, trivialPackage, and typosquat to `ignore` for this package and via a `*` rule for every dependency.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
